issues.legal_issue: A transfer of possession and tenancy rights to another entity through a court-sanctioned amalgamation can attract the ground for eviction based on transfer without the landlord’s written consent, regardless of the transfer’s voluntariness or its purpose.
material_facts: The original tenant’s undertaking in India was amalgamated with an Indian company under a scheme sanctioned by a court.
The scheme transferred the original tenant’s leases and tenancy rights to the Indian company, which thereafter occupied the premises and carried on business there.
The original tenant ceased to exist as a separate corporate entity from the effective date of the amalgamation.
The landlord had not given written consent to the transfer.
The foreign-exchange direction required a reduction in the original tenant’s equity capital but did not require amalgamation; the companies chose that method of restructuring.
issues.conclusion: The transfer brought the case within the statutory ground for eviction, and the eviction order was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1)(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act covers subletting, assignment, or otherwise parting with possession without the landlord’s written consent. Whether the transfer was voluntary, involuntary, or undertaken to comply with law is irrelevant. The Court relied on M/s. Parasram Harnand Rao v. M/s. Shanti Prasad Narinder Kumar Jain, M/s. General Radio and Appliances Co. Ltd. v. M.A. Khader, and Cox & Kings Ltd. v. Chander Malhotra. It also considered sections 391 and 394 of the Companies Act, 1956, and section 29 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, and distinguished Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Shyam Co-operative Housing Society, which concerned a transfer provided for by statute.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and tenant_transferred_possession_to_another_entity and transferee_occupied_premises and no_written_landlord_consent

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from rented premises.
predicates.tenant_transferred_possession_to_another: The tenant transferred possession of the rented premises to another entity.
predicates.transferee_occupied_premises: The recipient entity took possession of and occupied the premises.
predicates.no_written_landlord_consent: The landlord had not given written consent to the transfer of possession.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns rented premises transferred by a tenant to an occupying entity without the landlord’s written consent, the tenant is liable for eviction.

issues.legal_issue: A company cannot rely on lifting the corporate veil to claim that its transferor remains in existence and in possession when the company itself asks the court to disregard its corporate identity and no fraudulent or improper use of the corporate form is shown.
material_facts: The appellant company asked the Court to look through the corporate structure and treat the original foreign company as still in existence and in possession of the premises.
The original tenant had ceased to exist as a separate entity following the amalgamation, and the appellant company occupied the premises.
The appellant did not show that the corporate form had been used to commit fraud, illegality, or improper conduct.
issues.conclusion: The appellant could not obtain the lifting of its own corporate veil, and the Court treated the appellant as the entity occupying the premises.
issues.legal_principle: The separate corporate personality may be disregarded in limited circumstances, including to prevent fraud or improper conduct, protect public interests, or defeat evasion of legal obligations. The doctrine does not permit a company to ask the court to unveil its own corporate identity to support its position. The Court relied on Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co. Ltd. v. State of Bihar, Delhi Development Authority v. Skipper Construction Co. (P) Ltd., and the principles discussed in Aron Salomon v. Salomon & Co. Ltd. and Gower’s Principles of Modern Company Law.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from rented premises.
predicates.company_itself_invokes_veil_lifting: The company whose separate identity would be disregarded asks the court to disregard its own corporate identity.
predicates.no_fraudulent_or_improper_use_shown: The company does not show that the corporate form was used to commit fraud, illegality, or improper conduct.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding, when a company asks the court to disregard its own corporate identity and no fraudulent or improper use is shown, its veil-lifting argument is rejected.
